arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Michael McConnell argued for the Hornes. He stated the case involves difficult merits questions. He focused on whether a taking occurred. He discussed how to conceptualize and value the taking. He emphasized the complexity of the legal issues.

Paul D. Clement argued for the Department of Agriculture. He began by identifying the property allegedly taken. He noted the Hornes advanced two different theories. He argued the takings analysis must start with property identification. He challenged the Hornes' theories about property ownership.

Justice Sotomayor questioned the nature of the taking. She asked what is taken from the handler entity. She explored the distinction between ownership and handling. She noted the handler entity does not own the raisins. She asked if the taking is a percentage payment. She highlighted the legal distinction between the two entities.

Chief Justice Roberts managed the oral argument. He introduced the case and the parties. He called on the side that brought the case's counsel first. He set the stage for the merits discussion. He ensured the argument focused on the taking question.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Horne family challenges a federal marketing order. They argue the order forces them to pay for raisins they do not own. The Department of Agriculture defends the program. It claims the order regulates the raisin market. The core dispute involves the definition of property taken.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on March 20, 2013.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 9-19

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The Hornes want the Court to strike down the payment requirement. They argue the government takes property from a non-owner entity.
The Department of Agriculture wants the Court to uphold the marketing order. It argues the order validly regulates the raisin market.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 27, lines 9-31
Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 21-31

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The Hornes argue the government takes money from the handler entity. They claim the handler entity does not own the raisins. They assert this constitutes a taking of property.

The Department of Agriculture argues the order regulates the raisin market. It claims the payment requirement is a valid exercise of regulatory power. It asserts the order does not take property from the handler entity.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked what is being taken from the handler entity. She questioned whether two separate legal entities exist. One entity owns the raisins. The other entity handles the raisins. She asked if the handler entity owns the raisins. She noted that the handler entity cannot be taken raisins if it does not own them.

Chief Justice Roberts introduced the case. He called on the side that brought the case's counsel to argue. He identified the case as Horne v. Department of Agriculture. He noted the argument would focus on the merits. He asked the counsel to address the taking question.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The case defines the scope of government power over agricultural markets. It clarifies what constitutes a taking of property. It determines whether regulators can force payments from entities that do not own the underlying goods. The outcome affects how the government structures marketing orders. It impacts the rights of business owners in regulated industries.
